subject.title: [Feature]: Store configuration backup files in their own directory, with datetime name convention

question: Should OpenClaw make a dedicated `config-backup/` directory with datetime names the canonical config-backup layout, or keep adjacent backups and only change naming or documentation?
rationale: The change is feasible but alters the product contract for sensitive config recovery files, legacy `.bak.N` handling, audit output, and overlapping timestamp-only work, so automation should not choose the permanent layout alone.

options.title: Adopt Dedicated Directory Layout
options.body: Make this issue the canonical design and require a migration-safe implementation covering legacy adjacent backups, recovery, permissions, retention, audit text, doctor docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Limit Scope To Timestamp Suffixes
options.body: Keep backups adjacent and route naming-only work through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39923 and its linked PR, then narrow or close the directory request separately.

options.title: Keep Current Backup Ring
options.body: Reject the layout change for now and document the adjacent numbered backup ring as the intended stable behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt Dedicated Directory Layout
recommendation.body: Make this issue the canonical design and require a migration-safe implementation covering legacy adjacent backups, recovery, permissions, retention, audit text, doctor docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history on config backup and recovery semantics and already provided maintainer review context for this exact request.
